title: High-Nuclearity Lanthanide-Containing Clusters as Potential Molecular Magnetic Coolers
claim: Lanthanide hydroxide cluster assembly is too sensitive to ligand identity, ligand/metal ratio, anion templates, pH, temperature, and reaction time for reliable prediction, and clusters with nuclearity above 25 remain few despite recognized modular cubane-based motifs.
explanation: The outlook states that common modular features suggest “clusters of clusters,” including a hypothetical fullerene-like cage of five- and six-vertex-sharing [Ln4(μ3-OH)4]8+ wheels, but this is an ongoing target rather than a demonstrated synthesis. The same sensitivity is illustrated earlier by pH- and ion-dependent Ni–Ln products.
scope: Rational synthesis of giant lanthanide and 3d–4f hydroxide clusters for magnetic cooling.
caveats: The C60-like supercluster is a design proposal only. Magnetic-cooler performance still also requires high spin density, low anisotropy, and weak coupling, which are not guaranteed by nuclearity alone.
